title: Interval List Intersections
statement: Both lists are sorted and internally disjoint. Return every intersection between an interval of the first list and one of the second, in sorted order. Intervals that merely touch at a point still intersect, producing a single-point interval.
constraints: each list is sorted ascending and its own intervals never overlap
either list may be empty, in which case the answer is empty
hints: Comparing every pair is O(n*m) and ignores that both lists are already sorted.
Two pointers, one per list. The intersection of the two current intervals, if any, runs from the larger start to the smaller end.
That candidate is real exactly when start <= end. Then advance the pointer whose interval ENDS first, because it can never intersect anything later in the other list.
